target_customer: Consumers and knowledge workers managing everyday tasks
problem: Work is scattered across chats, inboxes and docs; to-do lists record tasks but do not do them.
business_model: Consumer subscription app (Mac and iOS) with an AI Operator
product_category: AI to-do list and personal assistant

founders.name: Tobias Eichenwald
founders.background_notes: Programmer and designer with three Red Dot Awards per YC page.

competitors.name: Todoist
competitors.what: To-do app that added AI voice task capture

technical_complexity.rationale: Agent execution inside apps and websites is hard, but the base app is standard engineering with modern LLMs.

defensibility.rationale: Incumbent task apps and general assistants can add the same agent features quickly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to say; Todoist shipped AI task capture in January 2026.

market_need_then: Founders argue AI assistants scattered work across chats and inboxes; launched October 6, 2026 per Digg.

brand_strength.rationale: A short place name with a brand marketing cofounder, but no press on the brand yet; the name is shared with Rome, AS Roma and other products.

outcome_analysis: Roma is a Fall 2026 company with three founders, two of whom had earlier YC exits, so its team is strong, but it only launched in October 2026. There is no verified funding or traction data, so the outcome is unknown and the record reflects founder signal only.
notes: Dealroom shows $125K seed and says Tobias Eichenwald founded Loom; YC says Jan Senderek founded Loom. Dealroom is marked made with AI, and Startup Seeker says funding is not disclosed, so no round is recorded. The YC page is the source for founder roles.
